title: Request lifecycle guardrails and hedge-orchestration spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Our services and SDKs have diverged in how they perform retries, hedged requests, timeouts and idempotency metadata. This causes inconsistent client behavior during multi-region failover, uneven SLO attainment across routes, and hard-to-debug duplication or silent data-loss risks. Goal: Define a single request-lifecycle contract and an "hedge-orchestration" pattern that unifies: timeout budgeting, retry/backoff envelope, hedged request windows, idempotency-key validation and propagation, circuit-breaker signals, and load-shedding hooks. The spec should be SDK-friendly (explicit primitives and sensible defaults), runtime-enforceable (headers and telemetry hooks), and support gradual rollouts with feature flags and per-route overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc reviewed and approved by Runtime, SDK, and Platform Reliability leads
SDK changes stubbed for Node/Python/Go with consistent API surface for idempotency key generation/propagation
Runtime implements header-level contract (X-Req-Lifecycle) that encodes timeout budget, hedge-window, and idempotency semantics
E2E test harness demonstrates no duplicate side-effects for idempotent flows under hedged fanout (0 flakiness across 1000 CI runs)
Two customer-facing routes rolled out behind feature flag with metrics: successful_requests, duplicate_side_effects, p99_latency, shed_count
Runbook snippets for on-call describing how to interpret guardrail telemetry and flip fallbacks
design_decisions: Use a compact header (X-Req-Lifecycle) for runtime-to-runtime portability; header encodes version, timeout_budget_ms, hedge_window_ms, idempotency_required flag
Default hedging policy: disabled for non-idempotent operations; for idempotent flows default hedge_window = min(30ms, 20% of per-request sla)

Timeout budgeting negotiated: client declares desired overall_deadline_ms; SDKs maintain per-hop budget computed from route profile; runtime enforces budget and rejects excessive hedging if budget is insufficient
Circuit-breaker integration: request-level tokens include a CB-allow flag; runtime can return 503+Retry-After when shedding is required; SDK interprets as soft-failure and records metrics
Telemetry: attach explicit trace tags for hedged requests (hedge_parent_id, hedge_attempt_index) to disambiguate duplicates in traces and logs
Idempotency: require explicit Idempotency-Key header for side-effecting endpoints; SDK helper to compute stable keys for commonly used primitives (createOrder, chargeCard)
tradeoffs: Embedding structured state in a header keeps runtime coordination simple but limits extensibility; future fields must be versioned to remain backwards compatible
Conservative defaults (small hedge windows) favor safety and lowered duplicate risk but may miss tail-latency improvements for some workloads
Enforcing idempotency keys at the SDK level improves correctness but may inconvenience non-SDK callers; documented fallback path provided
Strong runtime enforcement of hedging can increase observability overhead and trace cardinality; mitigations include sampled detailed traces and aggregate counters
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize spec and publish Confluence page; secure sign-off from Runtime, SDK, and Platform Reliability
Week 2: Implement header parsing and enforcement in runtime behind feature flag resilience.request_lifecycle_v1; add telemetry labels
Week 3: Land SDK helper libraries (Node/Python/Go) with opt-in feature flag and examples; publish migration guide
Week 4: Enable on low-risk internal routes (CI cache, metrics ingestion) and validate no-dup metrics and acceptable latencies
Week 5-6: Expand to customer-facing read-heavy routes with hedging enabled; monitor duplicate_side_effects metric closely; if >0.1% duplicates for idempotent flows, rollback hedging
Post-rollout: GA toggle and embed in runtime rollout policy with per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private deployments
